analysis.description: The Medical_Records table stores patient health metrics and diagnostic indicators for cardiovascular risk assessment and chronic disease management. It serves as a central repository for key biomedical data used in clinical decision-making and population health analysis.

columns.record_id: Unique identifier for each medical record entry
columns.patient_id: Reference to the associated patient in the Patients table
columns.cholesterol: Blood cholesterol levels measured in mg/dL
columns.blood_pressure: Blood pressure readings formatted as systolic/diastolic (e.g., 145/95)
columns.diabetes: Binary flag indicating diabetes presence (1) or absence (0)
columns.heart_disease: Binary flag indicating heart disease presence (1) or absence (0)

example_questions: Which patients have both diabetes and heart disease?
What is the average cholesterol level for patients with high blood pressure?
How many records show abnormal blood pressure readings?

analysis.description: The Patients table stores core demographic and health-related information for individuals under medical care, serving as a foundational dataset for tracking patient profiles and linking to their medical history and treatments.

columns.patient_id: A unique identifier for each patient, serving as the primary key for record management
columns.name: Full name of the patient, typically stored as a text string
columns.age: Patient's age in years, stored as an integer value
columns.gender: Biological sex of the patient, with possible values like Male, Female, or Other
columns.bmi: Body Mass Index calculated from height and weight, stored as a floating-point number
columns.smoker: Binary indicator for smoking status (1 for smoker, 0 for non-smoker)

example_questions: What is the average BMI among male patients?
How many smokers are recorded in the patient database?
What demographic patterns exist in the patient population?

analysis.description: The Treatments table stores information about medical interventions provided to patients, including medications, surgical procedures, and follow-up durations. It serves as a central repository for tracking patient treatment plans and their associated follow-up periods.

columns.treatment_id: A unique identifier for each treatment record, serving as the primary key
columns.patient_id: A foreign key linking to the Patients table, identifying which patient received the treatment
columns.medication: The name of the medication prescribed, with 'None' indicating no medication was administered
columns.surgery: The type of surgical procedure performed, with 'None' indicating no surgery was conducted
columns.follow_up_months: The duration in months of the follow-up period after treatment completion

example_questions: Which patients received surgery and what was the follow-up duration?
What medications were prescribed to patients with follow-up periods over 12 months?
How many treatments involved both medication and surgical procedures?
